summary:
At b7e9c18, all 14 acceptance criteria are met.

This lap changed only comments in src, plus PoolWatch.ps1, PoolWatchCases.ps1 and fitness.yaml. The diff does what O-110 to O-113 asked:
- O-110: `killed` is recorded only in the branch that kills, and the MISSING line has three wordings.
- O-111: Remove-StaleRehearsals runs at the start of -Rehearse, and the header states a 10-minute timeout.
- O-112: the comments now say 'while the precaution is on (Q-186)', and the leak is described per entry touched.
- O-113: C-011 filters processes by its own run folder.

Outside the repro and the design record's 'not settled' line, no first-touch or single-use claim is left, and nothing cites the deleted test. The architecture text the send-back calls AA-015 appears in this slice's record as AA-016. It says a root at or inside the store is refused while the precaution is on, and that with it off both the refusal and the exclusion are lifted. That matches Q-186, and the tests it rests on pass.

What I ran, with pool marks around each step: the repro (exit 0), ContainerLayerStoreTests (37/37), rules-parity (AGREE), the rules harness (93/93), Fitness (81 rules hold), WindowCases X-006, X-005, X-004, X-002, X-001 and T-003 (all passed), PoolWatchCases All (all 10 passed, including the C-052 rehearsal: RUN COMPLETE and the stale-folder sweep), WindowMutants -Mutant All (11/11 caught), and the full suite.

The full suite gave 537 passed and 3 failed. The 3 are the last-access tests that the build-check saw failing at afd021d, before this slice.

X-006 ran on this PC's live layer store through the published exe and gave WC* +0 and System 0x120089 +0. Over the whole session, V0 to the end, WCsc stayed at 3712, WCfc and WCri at 2886, FMwi at 3729 and 0x120089 at 3761. Paged pool went −27 MB and nonpaged +32 MB, so the kernel-memory budget was never close.

A data point for SC-128: when the rehearsal deleted its 30,150-folder tree, FMfn live fell by 118,863 and paged pool by 92 MB. That FMfn retention went away when the files were deleted, without a restart.

Loop shape, as the builder already named it: build attempts 3–5 and 7–9 were each sent back over harness text or edge cases, and attempts 8–9 changed src comments only. This validation finds nothing more to send back. G1 and G2 are on the backlog as SC-130 and SC-131.

Not reached: the person-run 5 full plus 5 cancelled C: scans after a Restart, and the tens-of-GB growth itself. Both now belong to SC-128.

criteria.criterion: 1. Scan C: (a root above the store) when the planted store holds a nested Files\Windows tree plus Hives, Bindings and dotnet.bcf
criteria.how: AScanAboveTheStoreStopsAtItAndCountsEverythingElse passed. On the real store, X-006 and X-002 through the published exe gave skippedStores=1, opensUnderExcludedStore=0 and WC* +0. The repro passes.

criteria.criterion: 2. Pick a scan root that is the store itself or a folder inside it
criteria.how: ARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsRefused passed (store, \L1, \L1\Files\Windows, deeper). On the real store, X-001 and X-006 gave outcome=refused with nothing read and WC* +0.

criteria.criterion: 3. Pick a scan root that spells the store another way (\\?\, trailing separator, letter case)
criteria.how: ARootInsideTheStoreInAnotherSpellingIsRefusedWithNoOpen passed (extended, trailing, lower, upper). X-006 refused the real store in lower case.

criteria.criterion: 4. Pick a scan root that reaches the store through a junction, a subst drive or an 8.3 short name
criteria.how: ARootThroughAJunctionIntoTheStoreIsRefused passed. Per O-089 it covers the junction, subst and 8.3 forms on a planted store. I did not check whether its 8.3 branch ran: it asserts only when cmd's %~s gives a distinct short form.

criteria.criterion: 5. Scan C: with siblings named 'Layers.', 'Layers ' and 'Layers2', and a 'Layers' folder elsewhere
6. Scan C: when no container store exists
criteria.how: WithNoStoreTheScanIsWhatItWasBefore and AnEmptyKnownFolderMeansNoStoreNeverEveryPath passed. Checked only with an absent planted store; Windows 10 was not reached.

criteria.criterion: 7. Scan with the protection turned off, over a planted store and a picked root inside it
criteria.how: WithThePrecautionOffARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsScannedAsPicked (3 rows) and WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsListedAndCountedLikeAnyFolder passed. Both match Q-186: off lifts the exclusion and the refusal.

criteria.criterion: 8. Show why a result is different: a C: scan whose store was skipped, and a refused pick
criteria.how: X-006 passed on the real store. OutcomeTitle reads 'Not scanned: …', and OutcomeDetail names wcifs.sys, microsoft/Windows-Containers#646 and the Settings checkbox. OutcomeNotes reads 'Not scanned, size not counted…', and the Unreadable tab header counts the store apart. X-004 and X-002 also passed.

criteria.criterion: 9. Turn the protection off: untick and answer No, then untick and answer Yes
criteria.how: X-005 passed. No keeps the box ticked. Yes unticks it and the button reads 'Settings (1 off)...'. The question states the consequence per entry until a restart, and a fresh launch shows none off.

criteria.criterion: 10. Run the pool protocol end to end: PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol -Rehearse over a generated %TEMP% tree
criteria.how: PoolWatchCases C-052 passed: RUN COMPLETE and scratch deleted. It swept the planted stale folder and kept the planted live one.

criteria.criterion: 11. Completeness check: an exe-full arm exited 70 with a null report
12. Completeness check: arms.jsonl lacks arms the plan names, including no exe arms at all
13. Completeness check: a cancel or close arm whose hook refused
14. Completeness check: an arm missing its /settled mark, or guard-stopped while a later arm started over it
criteria.how: PoolWatchCases C-056 passed. P-003 also passed, with the new F4 shape: interrupted after the exe exited, and never called killed.

obligations.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1 Invoke-ExeArm sets killed only after Kill(). Get-Missing distinguishes killed, exited (exit N) before /settled, and not recorded. P-003 passed with F2 (killed) and F4 (exit 0, not killed).

Remove-StaleRehearsals runs at the start of -Rehearse with a 1-hour cutoff, and the PoolWatchCases header states the 10-minute timeout. C-052 passed: the planted 2-hour-old folder was swept and the live one kept. Four leftovers from other sessions' killed runs (10:34–10:46) are under an hour old and are kept by design.

EntryKind, EntryClassifier, the ContainerLayerStoreTests summary and the fitness.yaml because-text are conditioned on Q-186 and say the leak is per entry touched until a restart. A grep finds first-touch wording only in the repro (kept unchanged) and in the design record's 'not settled' line. Parity AGREE, harness 93/93.
C-011 filters Win32_Process by a CommandLine containing its own run folder. C-011 passed in -Case All.
Discharged by the engine. My own run of the same command also exited 0 (1 passed), as corroboration only.

not_reached: The person-run PoolWatch session (-Prepare, Start > Restart, -Protocol) with real 5 full and 5 cancelled C: scans. The original report's DONE (c) rests on it, and it moved to SC-128 when the criterion was narrowed.
A whole-drive C: scan by the published exe with the fix on this PC. Whole-drive scans are the person's to run.

The tens-of-GB growth itself: FMfn, NtfF and File retention with the store excluded (spike #87, outcome C). That is SC-128's. A data point for it: when this session's rehearsal deleted its 30,150-folder tree, FMfn live fell by 118,863 and paged pool by 92 MB, with no restart.
`fltmc filters` on C:. It needs an administrator, and no named elevation operation runs it.
Root spellings that need system or network changes: a net-use drive letter mapped to \\localhost\C$, a hosts-file or DNS alias, and a share an administrator created over ProgramData.
Other live WCI stores (a running Windows Sandbox, Docker windowsfilter). Neither exists on this PC.
Windows 10, or a PC without containers. Criterion 6 was checked only with an absent planted store.
The precaution-off path on the real store. It is forbidden on purpose because it leaks until a restart, so it was checked on planted stores only.
Whether criterion 4's 8.3 branch actually asserted on this volume. The test asserts only when a distinct short name exists, and I did not inspect which branch ran.
